summary.description: DFD for the project on Poseidon X

threats.title: Modbus AI Captain ID spoofing
threats.description: Mobus TCP lacks of authentication and integrity: an attacker can easily spoof the AI Captain IP if it reaches the OT network by requesting the ID's of who is connetcted though the modbus tcp. Then it can erease the register table and proceed to interact with the targeted victim (ECU) by identifying itself as the legitimate AI Captain
threats.mitigation: Micro-segmentation over OT network + allow-list of function code depending on sender ID

threats.title: Modbus AI Captain no audit trail of  request
threats.description: Mobus TCP lacks of authentication and integrity: an attacker can easily spoof the AI Captain IP if it reaches the OT network by requesting the ID's of who is connetcted though the modbus tcp. Then it can erease the register table and proceed to interact with the targeted victim (ECU) by identifying itself as the legitimate AI Captain
threats.mitigation: To ensure the audit trail of request, the system should implement an append-only DB for the logs of participants, which is computed by a cryptographically signed logging ( so that in case of an issue it is possible to retrieve the identity of the sender).

threats.title: Modbus AI Captain DoS
threats.description: AI Captian might not be able to provide request to the ECU via the Modbus TCP if it flooded by request from other sensors.
threats.mitigation: Apply a threshold rate of request from all sensors so that the AI Captain will not be blocked by flooding. Interaction from different sensors requires to be managed according to their priority.

threats.title: Modbus AI Captain Injection
threats.description: AI Captian might receive Modbus data packet tampered by an attacker as this protocol lacks of integrity check and authentication. An attacker, performing as a MITM, can change the ECU response (e.g. letting the AI CAptain receiving a false velocity) .
threats.mitigation: Migro-segmentation of the OT network + NIDS monitoring

threats.title: Modbus AI Captain Eavesdropping
threats.description: Data flow directed to AI Captain is not encrypted over Modbus TCP, thus an attacker can sniff or eavesdrop any information from ECU to AI Captain if it has access to OT network.
threats.mitigation: Migro-segmentation of the OT network + NIDS monitoring

threats.title: Receiving false Position from GNSS
threats.description: Attacker that can access the physical connection between GNSS receiver and NAVUnit can impersonate the gnss receiver and send a fake position. this will lead the ECDIS to record and anlayze the area related to the fake position
threats.mitigation: physical access protection + NIDS + check coherency between last received positions

threats.title: NavUnit navigation info disclousure
threats.description: if NavUnit does not provide access control to the navigation DB, allowing the attacker to extract important information if it can access via physical or network level, or via the GNSS receiver and AIS receiver
threats.mitigation: enhanche security over NavUnit  network (NIDS + tamper evident cable + authentication between component)so unauthorized access will not be able to retrieve navigation documentation.

threats.title: GNSS position Lost
threats.description: If the GNSS is not working properly (because of physical attack, low signal or satellite jamming)  NavUnit will not receive a proper updated position which will result in a DoS as the navigation system would not work properly.
threats.mitigation: protection of GNSS receiver + use an IMU dead-rocking measurement to provide an inertial position until the connection with the satellite is restored

threats.title: NavUnit corruption because of gnss position
threats.description: If NavUnit receives a tampered or spoofed position from GNSS receiver l, this position  will currupt the ECDIS navigation system.
threats.mitigation: protection of GNSS receiver + use an IMU dead-rocking measurement to provide an inertial position until the connection to double check + alert if any incosistency arises

threats.title: ECDIS unauthorized access
threats.description: If an attacker can access the navigation network via LAN, the interface of the ECDIS and overpass its security,  it can obtain an elevation of privilege by being able to access the navigation unit as admin level. this it can overwrite the navigation chart, position and communication DB, disabling navigation alerts...
threats.mitigation: strong authentication for NavUnit management + firmware updated and verified + admin level accessible only from AI Captain or verified remote control.

threats.title: false AIS position
threats.description: VHF lacks of inegrity and authentication. Thus, an attacker can imitate another vessel to trick the PoseidonX into belivieng there is  or there is not an immidiate ship in a certain position.
threats.mitigation: implement also the usage of radar to double check

threats.title: ECDIS currupted by false AIS position
threats.description: if an attacker sends a fake position to AIS imitating the presence or the absence of a ship related to a certain position, the ECDIS navigation system will output decision based on uncorrect data.
threats.mitigation: double check with radar the surroundings + check for AIS tampering at physical and network level to avoid unauthorized access

threats.title: AIS communication Log lacking
threats.description: As VHF lacks of authenticity and logging, it is not possible to verify who is the author of a certain message. Thus, an attacker could imitate a certain ship, and that ship has no way to repudiate the attacker actions.
threats.mitigation: as the  AIS channel is meant to be public applying authentication process would distrupt the nature of this communication but it is possible to apply log using timestamps and WORM DB

threats.title: AIS communication lost
threats.description: AIS communication can be flooded by an attacker with false messages, so that the proper  communication between other vessels is interrupted. This could have catastrophical outcomes if our ship is not able to acknowledge the presence of an immidiate ship as the NavUnit wouldn't be able to use that info to calculate an emergency move
threats.mitigation: implement also the usage of radar to double check presence of immediate ships + maximum flow rate for ais receiver

threats.title: Satellite Communication Jamming
threats.description: Satellite communication works on L-Band frequency, which are very weak signaling. An attacker can overpower the legitimate signal by using stronger signal and impersonating the legitimate satellite. Thus, the received signal will not allow the receiver to alculate its position.
threats.mitigation: anti-jamming antenna + not relying on a single satellite but on a multi satellite constellation

threats.title: GNSS  satellite signal not authenticated
threats.description: Civillian Satellite signal is not verified by authentication nor digital signatur: thus, the receiver has no way to detect the legitimacy of the received signal.
threats.mitigation: enable cryptographic signing and logging over gnss

threats.title: GNSS  receiver tampering
threats.description: Internal/maintenance port of receiver might be subject to information disclosure attack as it might allow to retrieve internal information
threats.mitigation: physical access control to gnss receiver

threats.title: GNSS receiver Disconnection
threats.description: Physically disconnecting the receiver antenna will result in a D0s
threats.mitigation: Physical protection over intentional and unintentional reaceiver antenna

threats.title: GNSS receiver DoS
threats.description: DoS of GNSS receiver can be obtained by jamming the receiver antenna using overpowering signals
threats.mitigation: Anti-jamming antenna + multi satellite constallation

threats.title: Physically tampered GNSS receiver
threats.description: An attacker with physical access can modify the gnss receiver firmware so the ouput position will be inexact.
threats.mitigation: Physical access security check including periodic firmware check

threats.title: exploitation of firmware vulnerabilities
threats.description: Attacker can use malicious spoofed signal to exploit firmware vulnerabilities which might lead to a buffer overflow and thus the execution of malicious code
threats.mitigation: periodic firmware check and update + memory protection

threats.title: AI Captain Impersonation through Modbus
threats.description: Modbus TCP is protocol that lacks of authentication and encryption, thus if an attacker can apply spoofing to imitate a legitimate network component by sniffing its ID, to send un-authenticated data.
threats.mitigation: Micro-segmentation over OT network + allow-list of function code depending on sender ID

threats.title: AI Request Tampering
threats.description: As there is no authentication or check of integrity over a received request, an attacker can inject a legitimate AI Captain request and overide the function code to obtain a desired behaviour .

threats.title: ECU no audit trail of received request
threats.description: As authentication is not implemented in Modbus TCP the AI Captain suffers from insufficient logging: thus, it is not possible to check if a problematic request has been issued by a legitimate component or a malicious one.
threats.mitigation: To ensure the audit trail of request, the system should implement a DB for the requests and a logging process for the participants ( so that in case of an issue it is possible to retrieve the identity of the sender).

threats.title: PCL  ECU register overwriting
threats.description: As there is no authentication or check of integrity over a received request, an attacker can scan the OT network and find the PCL port. Thus, it can tamper a request from the AI Captain to override the PCL firmware by changing ECU register values.
threats.mitigation: Engineering port physically disabled at least during travelling + requires two-person authorization to physically access it.

threats.title: Accessing through Engineering port to  overide security logic of PLC
threats.description: As there is no authentication or check of integrity over a received request, an attacker can scan the OT network and find the PCL port and its hardware finger print.  Then it can use the vendor software to override completely the PLC logic.
threats.mitigation: Engineering port physically disabled at least during travelling + requires two-person authorization to physically access it.

threats.title: ECU overflooding
threats.description: As there is no authentication or check of integrity over a received request, an attacker can scan the OT network and find the PCL port and its hardware finger print.
threats.mitigation: Engineering port physically disabled at least during travelling + requires two-person authorization to physically access it.

threats.title: ECU Register Eavesdrop
threats.description: As there is no authentication or check of integrity over a received request, an attacker can access the ECU register values by sending/tampering a request to the ECU and using the Function Code related to the read holding register (e.g. current velocity, rpm...).
threats.mitigation: Apply an allowed-function code list over a OT Firewall in combination with a OT micro-segmentation: This will ensure that certain request (e.g write) will be allowed iff sent by the legitimate AI Captain, and that the data flows only through AI Captain and ECU and no futher entity.

threats.title: Vessels Position eavesdropping

threats.title: Modbus Injection
threats.description: Modbus TCP does not have any authentication protocol. Thus, it is possible for an attacker to inject maliciously the data flow between AI Captain and ECU, with the scope to alter the Engine Controller values and security threshold. This attack exploits the usage of the function code in Modbus Data Packet.
threats.mitigation: Apply an allowed-function code list over a OT Firewall in combination with a OT micro-segmentation: This will ensure that certain request (e.g write) will be allowed iff sent by the legitimate AI Captain, and that the data flows only through AI Captain and ECU and no futher entity.

threats.title: ModBus EavesDropping
threats.description: Modbus TCP is protocol that lacks of authentication and encryption, thus if an attacker can eavesdrop or sniff the data flow between components, it will understand every Modbus Data Packed content.
threats.mitigation: Network Micro-segmentation of OT will ensure that only authorized component can access the data flow over Modbus TCP ( e.g AI Captain and ECU)

threats.title: Modbus TCP Flooding
threats.description: Modbus TCP protocol, does not implement any threshold for the request rate over its channel. As this protocol works as a client-server protocol, a flooding request rate will result as a DoS
threats.mitigation: Implementing a safe threshold rate over the OT network firewall will ensure to avoid this attack.
